title: Memory participates in observable program state
proposition: An execution model can represent memory as addressable state that instructions read and modify, while distinguishing that abstraction from persistent storage and physical memory hierarchy.
scope: Introductory abstract-machine reasoning with WebAssembly and x86 documentation as concrete boundaries.
exceptions: Caches, virtual memory, persistence, and physical implementation remain outside V01-C02 scope.
score_rationale: Two independent official architecture/specification sources support addressable execution state; scope excludes physical and persistence details.
